name: New Year
title: New Year holiday ideas
intro: Big fireworks, northern lights or summer sunshine to see in the new year. Here's where to go on holiday for New Year's Eve, near and far.
seo_title: New Year holidays: where to go for New Year's Eve

sections.heading: First, decide what kind of night you want
sections.text:
New Year's Eve abroad can mean very different things, and picking the wrong one is the easiest way to be disappointed. Before you look at flights, agree on which of these you're after:

- **A huge public party** with crowds, music and fireworks at midnight.
- **Fireworks you can watch** without being squashed, ideally somewhere warm.
- **Something traditional** that feels local, not a generic party.
- **A quiet, beautiful escape** from all of it.

Also check your flights home. Flights on 1 January are often cheaper and quieter than 2 January, but nobody wants a 7am flight after midnight in the cold. Most of these places suit **three or four nights**, arriving on the 30th or 31st.

sections.heading: Madeira: the big fireworks, in the warm
sections.text:
[Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is the one to pick if fireworks are the point. Funchal's display is fired from dozens of spots around the bay and up the hillsides, so the whole amphitheatre of the city lights up at once. It was recognised by Guinness World Records as the largest fireworks display in 2006, and the midnight show usually lasts around eight minutes.

The big advantage is the weather: average highs are around 20°C in December, so you can stand outside in a light jacket. Because the city climbs the hills, you can watch from all over Funchal, including many hotel balconies, rather than battling for a spot by the water. Cruise ships also gather in the bay for the night.

The catch is price. It's Madeira's busiest week, so hotels and flights go up and the best-located rooms book early. Stay a week and you'll have time for the levadas too.

sections.heading: Vienna: the most elegant New Year's Eve
sections.text:
[Vienna](/destinations/vienna) does New Year's Eve with a bit of style. The Silvesterpfad, or New Year's Eve Trail, turns the streets and squares of the old centre into a free festival, with stages, food and drink stalls running from mid-afternoon until the early hours. At midnight, the bells ring out and you'll hear the Blue Danube waltz played across the city, and people really do dance in the street.

The next morning brings the Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert. Tickets are given out by a lottery run by the orchestra early in the year before and are very hard to get, so don't build a trip around it. Plenty of other concerts and balls run around New Year if you want to dress up.

It's cold, with highs of around 4°C, so pack properly. Three or four nights is ideal.

sections.heading: Reykjavik: bonfires and fireworks everywhere
sections.text:
[Reykjavik](/destinations/reykjavik) has one of the most unusual New Year's Eves in Europe. In the evening, locals gather at community bonfires around the city, usually lit around 8.30pm. Then most of the country goes home to watch the annual comedy review on TV, before heading out again as midnight approaches, when it feels as if the entire city is setting off fireworks at once.

The best view is from the hill around Hallgrímskirkja church, though it gets packed. Bonfires can be cancelled if it's too windy, so it's worth checking the city's website on the day.

It's dark for most of the day in late December, but that does give you a chance of northern lights on clear nights outside the city. Four or five nights lets you add a Golden Circle day trip.

sections.heading: Berlin: the biggest party
sections.text:
If you want a huge crowd, [Berlin](/destinations/berlin) is the place. The city's big party is usually held at the Brandenburg Gate, with stages, music and midnight fireworks. For the last New Year, entry was free but you needed a named ticket booked in advance and photo ID on the night, so check the details for this year early.

The rest of the city is just as loud. Germans buy fireworks in huge numbers, and parts of Berlin can feel chaotic after dark, which is exciting for some people and too much for others. If you'd rather keep your distance, book a dinner, a club night or a concert, or watch from a hotel window.

sections.heading: Copenhagen: hygge with a bang
sections.text:
[Copenhagen](/destinations/copenhagen) mixes cosy Danish traditions with a lot of fireworks. Danes sit down to a long dinner, many watch the monarch's New Year speech at 6pm, and at midnight there's a tradition of standing on a chair and jumping off into the new year. The crowd in the City Hall Square counts down with the big clock on the town hall.

It's a good choice for a group who want a big dinner and a midnight moment without a giant organised party. Book restaurants well ahead, as plenty close for the night or only offer set menus.

sections.heading: Lisbon and Tenerife: mild nights by the sea
sections.text:
If Madeira is too expensive or booked up, two other places give you a New Year's Eve outdoors without freezing:

- **[Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon):** the main party is on the riverside Praça do Comércio, with music and fireworks over the Tagus. Highs are around 15°C, so it's cool but comfortable, and it's an easy short-haul city break.
- **[Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife):** around 22°C, with resort parties and fireworks along the coast. Spaniards eat twelve grapes on the twelve chimes of midnight, one for good luck in each month of the new year, and you'll be handed some in most places.

Neither has quite the spectacle of Funchal, but both are a lot cheaper and easier to book late.

sections.heading: Amsterdam and Prague: check before you book
sections.text:
These two are famous for New Year's Eve, but things have changed recently, so check what's on before you build a trip around fireworks.

- **[Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam)** used to be known for fireworks going off all over the city. The Netherlands has voted to ban consumer fireworks, so expect far fewer street fireworks than in the past, and check the current rules. The city has put on a free light, laser and music show at Museumplein instead.
- **[Prague](/destinations/prague)** has stopped its official city fireworks display. The streets and Old Town Square still fill up with people at midnight, and it's still a lovely city in winter, but don't go expecting a big organised show.

Both are still great places to be at New Year. Just go for the city, not the fireworks.

sections.heading: Lapland or Tromsø: a quiet New Year
sections.text:
If you'd rather skip the crowds entirely, head north. [Rovaniemi](/destinations/rovaniemi) and [Tromsø](/destinations/tromso) offer snow, husky rides, reindeer and the chance of northern lights. Rovaniemi averages around -6°C in December and Tromsø about -1°C, and both are in the polar night, so there's little daylight.

There'll still be some fireworks at midnight, but the real draw is a quiet night outside under the stars. It's also a nice alternative to the much busier week before Christmas in Lapland, though prices stay high over New Year too. See our [Rovaniemi, Levi or Saariselkä](/blog/rovaniemi-levi-or-saariselka) comparison if Lapland appeals.

sections.heading: Which one should you choose?
sections.text:
- **Warm weather and the best fireworks:** Madeira.
- **Something elegant and traditional:** Vienna.
- **Something you won't do anywhere else:** Reykjavik.
- **The biggest party:** Berlin.
- **A long dinner with friends:** Copenhagen.
- **Mild and easy to book:** Lisbon or Tenerife.
- **Peace and quiet:** Rovaniemi or Tromsø.

For more ideas, including long-haul places like Sydney and Rio, see the guides above and [where to go in December](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december). If you're planning with a group who all want something different, add a few of these to a shared [somewhere.party](/) list and let the points decide.

faqs.question: Where has the best New Year's Eve fireworks?
faqs.answer: Sydney Harbour, Rio's Copacabana beach, Dubai's Burj Khalifa and Madeira's harbour at Funchal are famous for their fireworks. In Europe, Berlin, Prague, Amsterdam, Copenhagen and Reykjavik see in the new year with fireworks all over the city, and in Madrid the crowds in Puerta del Sol eat twelve grapes on the chimes of midnight.

faqs.question: Where can we go for New Year with young children?
faqs.answer: Somewhere you can watch fireworks early or from your hotel works best. Madeira's harbour fireworks can be seen from all over Funchal, and Tenerife resorts put on early family celebrations. Lapland and Tromsø are calm, snowy alternatives.

faqs.question: Where is warm for New Year?
faqs.answer: The Canary Islands are around 20 to 22°C. Further afield, Dubai is in its best season, and it's summer in Cape Town, Sydney and Rio de Janeiro.

faqs.question: Is New Year an expensive time to travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, along with Christmas it's the most expensive time of year, and hotels often have minimum stays over New Year's Eve. Book as early as you can, or go just after New Year, when prices drop.

faqs.question: Where in Europe has the best New Year's Eve fireworks?
faqs.answer: Funchal in Madeira is the best known, with a display fired from all around the bay that set a Guinness World Record in 2006. Reykjavik, Berlin and Copenhagen are also famous for fireworks, though much of those comes from residents rather than an official show.

faqs.question: Is Prague good for New Year's Eve?
faqs.answer: Prague is still a lively place to be at midnight, with crowds in the old town, but the city has stopped its official fireworks display. Go for the city and the atmosphere rather than a big show.

faqs.question: How far ahead should you book a New Year's Eve trip?
faqs.answer: As early as you can, especially for Madeira and Reykjavik, where hotels fill up and prices rise. For city breaks like Lisbon or Berlin, booking by October or early November usually still gives a reasonable choice.
